title: The Patient Winter
premise: Theo Dravenmoor takes a teaching post in the snowbound town of Hollowmere, where a class of students vanished in 1974 and the town has agreed, collectively, to remember nothing. He discovers that his late grandmother was the school's secretary that winter—and that every photograph in her house now shows an extra empty chair, one more each week. The chair is an invitation from whatever took the children, and it is counting down to him. To survive, Theo must uncover what the townspeople traded in 1974, return the thing they kept—a child's name no one will speak—and accept that saving himself means breaking the loyalty that keeps Hollowmere's survivors alive. In the end he speaks the name into the winter dark; the chairs vanish, the missing class walks out of the treeline aged not a day, and Theo leaves town carrying a memory the town will spend another fifty years trying to forget.
about_author: Gideon Whitlock is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine winters in towns small enough that everyone remembered what everyone else preferred forgotten. He writes horror about institutions, inheritance, and the bargains communities make with silence.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Theo arrives in Hollowmere to teach at Blackpine School, where the hallway photographs have careful gaps and the janitor counts doors aloud. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: uneasy belonging—he wants invisibility and senses the town offers it at a price.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk Roster
chapters.summary: Theo finds enrollment records listing eleven students for a classroom that holds ten desks, dated 1974. His questions make colleagues go flat and polite. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the first crack—curiosity curdling into the realization that silence here is enforced, not natural.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Album
chapters.summary: Sorting his grandmother Edith's house, Theo finds her 1974 staff photo—one face scratched out. That night, a plain wooden chair appears in the album's background where none was before. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: dread made domestic; grief entangled with fear.

chapters.title: What the Snow Keeps
chapters.summary: A student, Mara, tells Theo about 'the counting game' children play near the treeline, reciting names that stop one short. Theo follows the rhyme to a collapsed root cellar. POV: alternating Theo and Mara. Emotional beat: the horror passes to a child, raising stakes beyond himself.

chapters.title: The Secretary's Ledger
chapters.summary: In Edith's locked desk, Theo finds her ledger: attendance records ending mid-sentence, and a page torn out. A neighbor warns him that Edith 'paid her share' and so should he. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: betrayal—the person he loved most was complicit.

chapters.title: Twelve Chairs
chapters.summary: The photographs now show twelve chairs, and real chairs begin appearing in Theo's classroom overnight, arranged facing the window. The janitor confesses he counts doors because something once counted them back. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: siege mentality; the safe places are gone.

chapters.title: The Bargain of 1974
chapters.summary: Theo finds the torn ledger page hidden in a hymnal: the town traded one child's name to the winter to spare the rest during a famine-winter blizzard. Edith witnessed it and kept the name. POV: Theo with Edith's journal entries interleaved. Emotional beat: horrified understanding—survival was purchased, and the debt compounds.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Cold Arithmetic
chapters.summary: The town elders confront Theo: speaking the name breaks the compact and everyone protected since 1974 becomes claimable again. They offer him Edith's place in the arrangement if he stays quiet. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—loyalty as a hostage situation; truth as a weapon aimed at everyone.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: On the winter solstice, the thirteenth chair appears—with Theo's name carved into it. The school fills with cold, the doors won't stay counted, and the vanished class stands at the treeline waiting for their borrowed time to be settled. Theo drives through the storm to the root cellar. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve; he chooses truth over safety.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: In the cellar, Theo speaks the child's name—Wren Halloway—into the dark, returning what was taken. The chairs vanish; the eleven walk out of the snow unchanged while the town's long protection dissolves around them. Theo leaves Hollowmere as spring comes early. POV: Theo, closing with Mara. Emotional beat: costly grace—truth saved them all, but memory of the price will never thaw.
